blocks.text: India is the **world's most populous country (~1.4 billion)**. Its population is **unevenly distributed** — dense in fertile plains, sparse in mountains/deserts — and its **growth** is decelerating as India passes through the **demographic transition** (Census 2011 basis).

rows: Dense — Ganga plains, coasts, deltas; sparse — Himalayas, Thar, NE hills.
**Decadal growth 17.7% (2001-11)** — declining; TFR now below replacement (~2.0).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: population distribution & growth

items: **Census 2011**: India pop **1.21 billion** (2nd after China; likely 1st now, ~2023); **decadal growth 17.7%** (slowing); density **382/km²**; most populous state **UP**, least **Sikkim**, densest **Bihar (~1106)**, least dense **Arunachal**.
**Distribution**: dictated by **relief, water, soil, climate, industry** — dense **N. plains & coasts**, sparse deserts/mountains/forests.
**Demographic transition**: India in **Stage 3** (falling birth rate); **demographic dividend** window (~2018-2055) — median age ~28.
**AP (2011)**: population **~4.93 crore** (post-bifurcation residuary), density ~308/km²; ~70% rural; growth decelerating.
Policies: **National Population Policy 2000** (TFR target 2.1 — replacement level, now ~2.0 nationally, achieved).
Density 382/km² (Bihar highest); decadal growth 17.7% (2001-11); UP most populous state.
Distribution driven by relief, rainfall, soil, water, urbanisation.

blocks.text: Population composition — **sex ratio, literacy and the occupational (work) structure** — reveals the quality and character of the workforce. India shows an **improving but adverse sex ratio, rising literacy, and a still-large but shrinking primary-sector workforce** (Census 2011).

rows: **Primary (agriculture) ~cultivators+labourers largest share; secondary (industry); tertiary (services) rising**; main vs marginal workers.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: sex-ratio, literacy, occupation

items: **Sex ratio (Census 2011)**: India **943** (females/1000 males); highest **Kerala (1084)**, lowest **Haryana (879)**; **child sex ratio (0-6) fell to 919** (a concern → **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**).
**Literacy (2011)**: India **74.04%** (male 82.1%, female 65.5%); highest **Kerala (94%)**, lowest **Bihar (~62%)**; gender gap narrowing.

**Occupational structure**: workers = **main + marginal**; **primary (agriculture) ~ largest share of workforce** but falling; secondary & **services (largest GDP share)** rising; **feminisation of agriculture**; low female LFPR (~a key concern).
**AP**: sex ratio ~**993** (better than national); literacy ~**67%** (below national avg — a focus area).
Sex ratio 943 (Kerala highest, Haryana lowest); literacy 74% (Kerala highest, Bihar lowest).
Occupational shift: primary → tertiary; AP sex ratio (~993) is favourable.

blocks.text: India's population includes large **Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST)** communities and remains **majority rural**, though **urbanisation is rising**. These components shape welfare policy and India's social geography (Census 2011).

rows: **~16.6%** of population; highest share **Punjab**; listed under **Article 341**.
**~8.6%**; highest share **Mizoram/Lakshadweep**; most in absolute terms **MP**; **Article 342**.
SC ~17%, ST ~5-6%; ~70% rural; agency (tribal) areas in the Eastern Ghats.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: SC/ST & rural-urban composition

items: **SC (2011)** = **16.6%** of India; **ST = 8.6%**; SCs spread across plains, STs concentrated in **forest/hill 'tribal belt'** (central India, NE, Jharkhand-Odisha-Chhattisgarh).
**Rural-urban**: India ~**69% rural, 31% urban (2011)** — urbanising; the **level of urbanisation** highest in Goa/Tamil Nadu/Kerala.

**Tribes**: **PVTGs (Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups)** — 75 groups (e.g., Chenchus, Konda Reddis, Yanadis in AP); protected under the **Fifth Schedule & PESA (1996) & Forest Rights Act (2006)**.
**AP**: SC ~**17%**, ST ~**5.3%** (concentrated in the Eastern Ghats agency areas — Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, East Godavari); tribes — Koya, Konda Reddi, Savara, Yanadi, Sugali/Lambada, Chenchu.
Punjab highest SC share; MP most STs (absolute); AP ~70% rural.

blocks.text: India is an **extraordinary mosaic of races, tribes, religions and languages** — a **'unity in diversity'**. Its people are a deep intermixture; **Hinduism is the majority religion**; and it has **22 scheduled languages** across four major families.

rows: **22** in the 8th Schedule; most-spoken **Hindi**; **Telugu** among the largest Dravidian.
**~700+ Scheduled Tribes**; Gonds, Bhils, Santhals largest; AP — Koya, Chenchu, Savara.
Old typologies (Negrito, Proto-Australoid, Mongoloid, Mediterranean, Nordic) — of historical interest only.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: racial, tribal, religious & linguistic groups

items: **Racial groups (Herbert Risley)**: Negrito, Proto-Australoid, Mongoloid, Mediterranean, Western Brachycephals, Nordic — India = a 'melting pot'.

**Language families**: **Indo-Aryan (~74%)**, **Dravidian (~24% — Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam)**, **Austro-Asiatic (Munda, Santhali)**, **Tibeto-Burman (NE)**; the **8th Schedule** lists **22 languages** (Telugu is a **classical language**); **Hindi & English** = official Union languages.
**Religions (2011)**: **Hindu 79.8%, Muslim 14.2%, Christian 2.3%, Sikh 1.7%, Buddhist 0.7%, Jain 0.4%**.

**AP**: **Telugu** (official; classical language) predominant; sizeable Urdu-speaking & tribal-language communities; Hindu-majority with Muslim & Christian minorities (higher Christian share in some coastal/tribal districts).
Religion shares (Hindu 79.8%, Muslim 14.2%); 22 scheduled languages; 4 language families.
Treat 'race' cautiously (outdated). AP: Telugu + agency tribes.

blocks.text: **Urbanisation** — the rising share of people in towns and cities — is transforming India, driven by **migration** for jobs and services, and producing large **metropolitan regions**. It brings economic opportunity alongside challenges of slums, congestion and services.

rows: **31.2% urban (2011)**, rising; class-I cities & million-plus cities growing fastest.
**Rural→urban (dominant), urban→urban, inter/intra-state, international**; causes — economic pull, distress push.
**Million-plus cities**; mega-cities (>10 m) — Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata; census towns rising.
**Slums, congestion, water/sanitation, pollution, informal sector**; AMRUT/Smart Cities respond.
Urbanising around **Visakhapatnam (largest), Vijayawada-Guntur (capital region)**; loss of Hyderabad (2014).

items: **Urbanisation**: driven by industrialisation & services; **census towns** vs statutory towns; **million-plus cities** (~53 in 2011); **class-I towns**; issues — slums, congestion, pollution, waste.

**Migration (Census/PLFS)**: types — rural-urban (dominant for work), urban-urban, marriage (largest cause overall, esp. female); **push** (poverty, unemployment) & **pull** (jobs, education) factors; interstate migration to Maharashtra/Delhi/Gujarat.
**Metropolitan/urban schemes**: **Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, PMAY-Urban, Swachh Bharat**; census 'urban agglomerations'.

**AP metros/cities**: **Visakhapatnam** (largest city, port, executive-capital plan), **Vijayawada** (commercial), **Guntur, Nellore, Tirupati, Kurnool, Rajahmundry, Kakinada**; the **Amaravati** capital-region project; **Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor** driving urban growth.
31.2% urban (2011); rural-urban migration dominant; mega-cities >10 million.
Challenges: slums/services; AP urbanises around Vizag & Vijayawada-Guntur.
